title: MR MIGHTY trial_Evaluation and optimization of MR-guided microwave ablation (MWA) of liver tumors avoiding ionizing radiation
summary: MRI has the advantage over image guidance on a computer tomograph (X-ray) that the target (the tumor to be targeted) is displayed more precisely and can therefore be targeted more accurately. This is expected to lead to an improvement in therapy and a reduction in complications. Image-guided interventions on the liver under MRI guidance are routinely performed in our clinic.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of liver and intrahepatic bile ducts
Secondary malignant neoplasm of liver and intrahepatic bile duct

interventions.name: Patients who meet all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria may be proposed for the study and the patient will be informed about the study and the procedure. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Clinical indication for local ablative therapy of liver tumors (liver metastases or primary liver tumors). The indication for intervention in this case must be independent of the presented study.
No contraindication to MRI examination.
Size of the lesion ≤3cm
Exclusion criteria:
Contraindications to MRI examination, especially implants not suitable for MR, tattoos or piercings, limiting claustrophobia.
